sections: A picker for the agents that answer your asks: every engine, model, machine, effort and weight the host knows, plus councils, and crews of several agents working on one ask.

It reads the engine catalogue the host already keeps (no model is loaded and no machine is asked while it opens), lets you build a crew, and shows the exact Symblic text it will write. Nothing runs from the picker: the agents work only when you press Run, through the same admission paths as always.

Each agent becomes applicator text: engine:model@node, plus +effort and *weight when you set them. One agent can be the default for the whole run. Several agents answer one ask together: Vote collects answers and tallies them, Escalate tries them in order and keeps the first answer that passes the checks, Search runs checked attempts in parallel and keeps the passing one with the fewest attempts. A council (panel, debate, chain or layers) is a whole council of the host's agents answering one ask. Agreement between agents is reported, never treated as proof: only the checks accept an answer.

Search by model, maker or machine and add an agent. Local models are grouped by maker. Set supported effort and vote weight, then choose One agent, Vote, Escalate or Search. Check the machines refreshes the host installed tags and eligible worker nodes without loading a model. Each model choice retains its exact node identity.

The Symblic text box shows exactly what will be written. "Use for the whole run" sets the run default (asks with their own by keep theirs). "Apply to the ask at the cursor" adds the text to the ask your cursor is on, only when that ask has no by or with yet. "Insert as a group" adds a group line you can name in any ask with by crew. "Copy text" copies it for your own edit.

Owner-only catalog. Missing or failed metadata is visible. Saved installed tags remain visible without claiming readiness; use Check the machines to refresh. Embedding-only artifacts and models exceeding an observed memory limit are disabled. Cloud agents need the run cloud opt-in. Explicit @host choices use local admission. Ask edits still require a native program and an ask without its own by or with.

sections: The program editor with live colouring.

Every keystroke updates the draft, repaints the colours and schedules the static check. The text is sent to the server only for checking (and later for the action you press); it never reaches a model by typing.

A transparent textarea sits over a coloured copy; lines do not wrap and both scroll together. Colours: keywords bold accent; types such as Int and Text dotted-underlined; strings green; numbers amber; '#' comments grey italic; operators; capitalised logic variables italic on rule/query/holds lines. A whole line in grey 'prose' colour does not start with a keyword or a formal character: in the legacy profile such a line becomes an implicit model question, and the explicit and verified profiles reject it. 'program', 'note', 'section', 'module' and 'workflow' lines keep the rest of the line as prose. Every statement ends with a single period; a statement may continue over several lines.

Font 16 px; Tab inserts two spaces; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter = Run; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter = Preview; F8 = next problem; Shift+F8 = previous problem. Native source limits and the bounded editor-check byte limit remain visible failures.

Syntax colors remain separate from the checker. Red wavy underlines mark source errors; amber marks warnings. Editing clears stale underlines while the new source check is pending.
A misspelled keyword is an error, for example '"shwo" is not a keyword: did you mean `show`? (as written, the line would be sent to a model as a natural-language instruction)'.

sections: Source errors and warnings shown both as underlines and as an accessible problem list below the editor. Available in native Write, paper mode and English statements.

Shows the latest source checker messages with their original source locations. Click or tap a problem, press F8 for the next, or Shift+F8 for the previous. Typing clears stale results. No model is called and no program or external action is started by these source checks.

Errors block Run, Compare agents, Tighten and Crystallise ('Fix the errors first'); warnings do not. Errors include syntax ("unexpected '.' (a statement ends with a single period)"), names ('x is bound twice (Symblic names are immutable)', 'x may not be bound here: only some branches of the if at line N bind it (bind it in every branch, or add an else)', 'x is a builtin function name'), types, 'effort must be one of low, medium, high, max, ultra', vote-option errors and effects placed where a retry could repeat them. Warnings include 'x is read before anything binds it', '"roughly" is vague; a formal statement says exactly what it means', SYM_VACUOUS (the checks accept an empty answer) and other lint.
The current editor source. Click or tap a problem to select its location; F8 and Shift+F8 cycle problems while the editor has focus. Hover an underline for its explanation on desktop.

Red marks errors and amber marks warnings; each problem also names its severity in words. Exact token spans are used only when available. Whole-line positions, insertion points and unavailable locations are labeled honestly. A source check is not a runtime result or a proof that the program achieves your objective.

Parsing can stop at the first syntax error. Diagnostics and source sizes are bounded; truncation is visible. If checking is unavailable, it is reported as unavailable. Older servers can still supply the existing Write diagnostics without inline ranges. The bounded pure static lint can inspect predicates, but it does not execute a program or a provider.
'let a = b + 1.' gives the warning 'b is read before anything binds it'; 'shwo a.' gives the keyword error above.

sections: The green 'checks' badge with 'N statements · M asks', and the coloured determinism-profile bar with its class pills.

Summarises how each statement's result will be decided. exact (green): the kernel computes it. closed (accent): a model chooses from a small finite set (Bool, one of {…}, an Int range of at most 1,001 values, records of those). structured (amber): a model gives a canonical but open value (numbers, lists, records). open (grey): free text or code. observed (accent): a capability read. effect (red): delegate or act, which change something outside.

N counts every plan row, including program, note and use lines and statements inside blocks; M counts ask statements. Bar widths are shares of statements. A class describes the mechanism, not the probability of a correct answer.
The badge appears only when the check passes.

sections: The run's default applicator: which agent or model answers every ask that does not name its own.

The searchable catalog selects one default applicator for Run, Preview, Crystallise and Send to Studio. Installed models such as DeepSeek and lighter Ollama models are discovered with their exact tags and node names. Compare, Tighten and Build retain their own selections. Selecting a model starts no model or agent.

For each ask the applicator is chosen in this order: the ask's own 'with by=…', then a program default 'use by=…', then this picker. Because the page always sends a picker value, 'use applicator=', 'use provider=' and 'use model=' only matter outside the page. Each engine is reached only through registered paths: Claude, Codex, agy and Copilot through host_agents.launch on a worker node where the fleet layer's probe shows that CLI signed in (the CLI then calls its cloud provider; the run records your cloud opt-in), with the answer schema passed to the CLI's structured-output flag and the ask's effort mapped low→low, medium→medium, high→high, max and ultra→max (codex max→xhigh; agy gets an effort only when a model is named, and never max; copilot never gets one); Ollama through host_agents on a worker node that has the model and where it fits that worker node's memory limit (fewest calls in flight, then the fleet's placement; never the host unless you write @host), schema as grammar-constrained output, first sample at temperature 0 and later ones at 0.7 with seed 7+i; ChatGPT and Gemini through the browser daemon on the host, one window at a time per run; a council through the host agent hub's start route with a hub template, its CLI and Ollama members moved to the worker nodes, stopped after it answers. A call waits up to 30 minutes for room (reading the fleet layer's active runs before launching); worker nodes at 85 °C or more get no new call until below 75 °C; a call may take 15 minutes (CLIs), 60 minutes (Ollama) or 4 hours (councils).

Search by model, maker or machine, then select a discovered applicator. Check installed models refreshes the local manifest and eligible worker node capability observations only when clicked. Models on this computer explicitly name @host; unpinned Ollama text uses worker node placement. Choose agents opens the crew/council editor. The manual field below remains available.

The selector and manual field show the same exact applicator. Installed tags survive host restarts and failed refreshes, but saved tags do not establish current readiness. Embedding-only models and models known to exceed a node memory limit stay visible and cannot be selected as ask applicators. Execution always rechecks admission.

Problems appear during the run, not when you click: 'no worker node has <model>' (Ollama) or 'no worker node has <cli> signed in' (agent CLIs), followed by '; name a node (e.g. "claude@node-a"), or "@host" to run it on this machine on purpose'; 'every worker node with <kind> is at 85.0 °C or more; still hot after N s'; '<kind>@<node>: still busy after N s'; "no council template 'x' (templates: …)". With the strict identity policy on, every non-Ollama chip's answers are refused.

Select deepseek-r1:1.5b · the host after checking installed models. The manual field becomes ollama:deepseek-r1:1.5b@host. Preview shows which model would receive each ask; Run uses the existing admitted local execution path.

sections: How to put several agents on the same statement: a group or list applicator on an ask plus voting, ultra, escalation, search or council options. The picker cannot do this; the program text can.

For one ask, each listed applicator answers in its own fresh context (only the from/context values you give it). Answers are type-checked, repaired up to 'retries' times, and combined by consensus on their canonical fingerprints; an 'ensure … else retry because …' check re-asks with feedback when it fails; the winner is bound, and the next statement starts from that formally established value.

'group g = [...]' (or a list in by=[...]) names the members. votes is at least the number of members and at most 25 per ask. effort=high asks 3 times, max 5, ultra 5 and then a second round in which each member sees up to 6 anonymised candidate answers with reasons and answers again (the second round decides). agree=0.8 sets the winning share; strict fails a contested ask (the verified profile always refuses contested votes); families=N requires support from N model lineages; ahead=k stops once one answer leads by k; vote=fields votes a record field by field; vote=median with within= for numbers; key=eval(it) groups answers by meaning; permute=K re-asks with options rotated; ambiguous=true asks each member for other readings (fail stops the run). route=escalate tries the members in order and keeps the first answer that passes the anchored ensure (cheap local models first, cloud last). route=search with samples and rounds runs checked candidates in parallel and keeps the pass with the fewest attempts (lowest index on ties). by='council:debate' runs a full council of the host's agents for that one line. Weights: {app: 'x', weight: 2} or 'x*2'. A run makes at most 4 calls at a time (API 1-8, not on the page), and each worker node runs one Ollama model at a time, so a large panel is limited by cluster capacity.

group, by=, votes, effort, agree, strict, families, ahead, vote, within, key, permute, ambiguous, route, samples, rounds, retries, weight; 'use by=panel, effort=ultra.' applies them to every later ask.
Runs → Statements: agreement bar and percentage, 'N answers' with each member's answer, node, round and time, a 'contested' pill when the vote was weak; escalation receipts in the Determinism panel.

'route=escalate requires an anchored ensure ... else retry with only kernel expressions and let bindings; no routines or effects'; 'route=escalate does not use voting options: …'; 'X: the applicators did not agree (agreement 50% < 80%)'; 'no applicator gave a valid answer for X (…)'.

group panel = ['ollama:qwen3:4b-instruct', 'ollama:gemma3:4b', 'ollama:phi4-mini'].
given city: Text = 'Paris'.
ask country: one of {France, Germany, Italy} 'Which country is {city} in?' with by=panel, effort=ultra
show country.

sections: One box per 'given' statement, under the heading 'Inputs'.
Values typed here are sent as the program's inputs with Preview, Run, Compare agents and Tighten. Nothing is stored on the server until a run starts (then they are kept in that run's meta.json).

Each box shows the input's name, its declared type ('any' if none) and either a red 'required' badge (no default) or 'empty = the default'. Text that starts with [ or { or a digit or a minus and digit, or is exactly true or false, is parsed as JSON (falling back to plain text); anything else is sent as text. Empty boxes are left out, so the default applies. The runner then converts the value to the declared type.
In the run, the given's row shows the note 'input' or 'default'.

Missing required input: the run (or Preview) fails with 'the input name is required (pass it when you run the program)'. Wrong type: 'n must be a number only, with no unit, currency, percentage or explanation; encode units explicitly, got "3 apples"'. 'Inputs are too large.' (over 200,000 characters).
With 'given city: Text = 'Paris'.' the box reads 'city Text empty = the default'; type Berlin and Run uses Berlin.
topics.doubts: Confirmed by code and a coercion probe: after Runs → Open program in editor or a Logic hand-off, text inputs are shown JSON-quoted ("Paris") and re-sent with the quote characters, so a Text input receives the quotes. Typing true into a Text box sends a Boolean, which becomes the text 'True'. Inputs survive a reload only for programs opened from a run or from Logic; otherwise they live in page memory. Values for deleted inputs are still sent and ignored.

When ticked, delegate statements may run: each starts a host agent (the three-agent pipeline, Claude Code, Codex …) through the hub's POST /api/agents/start and binds {id, engine, name, status, link}. An intent and an outcome are written to delegate-effects.jsonl before and after starting it, so a resumed run reuses a completed start instead of starting another, and an uncertain one is refused. Options such as model=, effort=, roles= and node= are passed to the hub.
The delegate row in Statements shows the agent id; the link opens the host's agent page.

sections: A checkbox 'Require matching recorded model identities'.

Adds model_pins='strict' to the run. Under strict, an answer is accepted only when its call carried an observed, freshly validated model-manifest digest equal to the first digest this run folder pinned for that applicator; everything else is refused before it is accepted or cached ('<applicator>: answer refused under model_pins=strict (<status> identity): <reason>'). Dispatched calls still count against the budget. Unticked (the default), identities are recorded and reported but never refuse an answer.

Only Ollama calls produce observed digests: the fleet layer's helper reads the Ollama model listing before and after the request. Claude, Codex, agy and Copilot report 'provider_reports_no_weight_digest', ChatGPT and Gemini 'web_reply_reports_no_weight_digest', councils 'composite_applicator_not_observed'. So under strict only Ollama applicators can answer; asks the kernel solves need no model. A different digest later in the same folder is drift: refused under strict, recorded otherwise. The choice is kept for this browser tab (sessionStorage 'symblic-v3-model-pins'); opening a strict run in the editor turns it on.

Checkbox. It is disabled, with the text 'This server does not support the strict policy. A selected strict policy blocks Run until the server supports it or you clear the selection.', when GET meta does not report features.strict_model_pins. The live code reports it available.
Runs → Determinism → Model manifest observations then says 'Answers with changed, missing or uncheckable manifest observations are refused. Dispatched calls remain charged.'

Page: 'Strict model identities require a server update. Your selection has been retained.' Server: 'Strict model identity enforcement needs the server update; no run was started.' and 'model_pins must be strict when supplied; omit it for recorded observations.' With the default picker (claude:haiku) every ask fails under strict.
Tick it, choose 'Qwen3 4B · worker nodes' and Run the starter: legs is accepted only with an observed digest, and the report lists ollama:qwen3:4b-instruct with 'observed: 1'.

sections: An optional, off-by-default setting for native programs: before an ask goes to a model, try to construct its value from the program's own ensure checks.
When on, Run sends options.constructor (linear or linear_diagnose), determine=false, solve=false and max_calls. Off, the Run request is exactly what it was before this setting existed.

Supported asks are Bool, Int or fraction values constrained by linear ensure checks (sums, constant multiples, comparisons) and flat records. A bounded worker proposes a value; Symblic checks it with the original native type and ensure predicates and only then binds it. linear binds a checked value; linear_diagnose only records candidates while models still answer. Attempts, time and solver work use the server's fixed bounds.

The checkbox, and under Advanced the mode and 'Model calls allowed for this run' (a whole number from 0 to 10000; 0 means no model fallback). The choice is kept for this browser tab (sessionStorage 'symblic-v4-constructor').
A constructed answer reports answered_by constructor with zero model votes. With 0 model calls, an ask the constructor cannot build fails the run and the run shows the failure.

Shown only as available when GET meta reports features.constructor_options; otherwise a selected setting blocks Run until it is cleared or the server is updated. A paper (.symd) and a task opened with its own run policy (Logic, a delegated contract, a reopened run) run unchanged, with the reason shown. The host must provision the pinned solver separately; the meta marker reports the API, not the solver.

The editor text, the Inputs and the picker.

sections: Starts a real, durable run and opens it in Runs. The server creates automation_data/symblic/runs/<12-hex id>/ with program.sym and meta.json (private files) and launches a user unit symblic-<id> in the host's work slice (MemoryMax 600M, CPUQuota 50%, nice 10, idle IO) running symblic/kernel/run.py on the host. The server re-checks the program, validates inputs and the applicator, and records options: the profile from 'use profile=', the picker as default by, model_pins, side_effects, and, when the program was opened from a run or from Logic and is still identical, that run's saved options (max_asks, max_calls, parallel, max_steps, execution pins). Editor text, Inputs, picker, side-effects box, identity policy.

Starts one complete, independent run of the same program and inputs per ticked applicator, each with that applicator as its default and its own folder and unit; saves a comparison record (automation_data/symblic/compare/<id>.json) and opens Compare, which lines up every statement's fingerprint across the runs.

topics.title: Tighten…
topics.where: #syTighten 'Tighten…', symblic-page.js:300; openTightenSheet 569-600; server start_tighten integration/host/symblic_engine.py:703-757; job symblic/authoring/tighten.py run_job 743-790, tighten 559-630, analyse 88-142, clarify 248-275
sections: A sheet 'Tighten with agents': panel checkboxes (chips except councils) and a Clarifier choice.

Starts a background job (unit symblic-tighten-<id>) that answers every ask once per panel member, finds the asks they read differently, asks the clarifier to rewrite those instructions with explicit assumptions (never the answer), and probes again. It produces a candidate program. It never changes your editor, your saved programs or the original. Opens the Tighten screen.

Each probe runs the whole program with every ask answered by every member at temperature 0 in a fresh context, each also listing other readings. Diagnoses per ask: converged; format (fewer than 60% of answers fit the type); ambiguous (enough readers list other readings, strong engines disagree, or a deviating answer matches a listed reading); capability (strong engines — claude, codex, agy, copilot, gemini, chatgpt, council — agree and weaker ones deviate); divergent; unreached (every reader unavailable); failed. Ambiguous, divergent and capability asks are clarified, but only if their instruction has no {expression}. A rewrite that names the most common answer is refused; a candidate must keep the rest of the program identical and pass the static check. Up to 2 rewrite rounds (3 probes). Deterministic suggestions (one of {…}, rounding places, record fields, worked examples) are added without a model. The result pins the original, candidate and audit SHA-256.

Panel: at least 2, at most 8 used; defaults Claude Haiku, Codex, Antigravity, Qwen3 4B, Llama 3.2 1B. Clarifier: claude:sonnet (default), claude:opus or codex. Inputs from the Inputs boxes. Rounds are not on the page (server default 2, maximum 3).

'Fix the errors first'; 'Tighten works on a program; compile the paper first (bin/symblic paper compile)'; 'Tick at least two'; 'The program has no ask: there is nothing for agents to read differently.'; 'Tightening needs at least two agents to compare.'; '<x>: unknown applicator …'; 'clarifier: …'; 'The tightening did not start.'

ask km: Number 'How far is a marathon?'
show km.

Shows each statement in order with its line, label, class, type, the names it reads and its options; asks also show their instruction (first 200 characters, with {…} where a value is inserted). Read-only; it uses the latest static check (running one if needed); no model.

topics.title: Determinism determinacy

sections: 'Answer determination': whether each executed ask's written checks pin down one answer.

Shows totals 'determined · underdetermined · contradictory · unassessed', and per ask 'Line N [· item k] · name: One answer satisfies the encoded constraints | Several answers satisfy the encoded constraints | No answer satisfies the encoded constraints | Uniqueness was not established'; for assessed asks 'Passing values: N · domain size: M · method: enumeration'; for unassessed asks the reason; 'Answered by: Kernel | Model | No accepted answer · solve mode: on | off | auto'; and 'Values admitted by the checks' (up to 20).

With determination enabled (the default), when an ask's type has at most 20,000 possible values (Bool, one of, Int ranges, small records, sets or fixed-length lists) and its anchored ensure uses only kernel builtins, the kernel tests every candidate against the checks before any model call. Exactly one passing value with solve=true (or only kernel applicators) means the kernel answers with zero calls; no passing value fails the run before any call ('X: no value in the declared domain satisfies its encoded predicates'). Unassessed reasons: No finite answer domain; Domain exceeds the analysis limit; No anchored checks; Check is outside this analysis (functions, routines, adapters); Analysis budget reached; Analysis was not attempted (for-each asks). The strict Boolean option determine=false disables pre-dispatch enumeration and empty-answer probes; its receipt is unassessed / author_disabled. Returned answers still face their ordinary checks. It conflicts with enabled solve or a kernel-only applicator.
This panel is read-only. In source or host defaults, determine=false disables determination; solve requests kernel construction when determination can establish one admitted answer.

→ 'One answer satisfies the encoded constraints · Passing values: 1 · domain size: 9 · Answered by: Kernel · solve mode: on' (probe: value 3, zero calls).

sections: A form that turns premises and a goal written in controlled logic into a proof task that a model must solve and the kernel then checks step by step.

Propositions are quoted sentences treated as opaque atoms; connectives and, or, implies and not (not A = A implies false), precedence not > and > or > implies, implies groups to the right. The model constructs an intuitionistic natural-deduction derivation; the host checker accepts it only if every step follows from your named premises and the conclusion exactly equals your goal. A passed proof is conditional on your premises (their truth and consistency are not checked); failing to find one does not make the goal false.

Flat proof steps: one answer with a list of inferences {id, rule, args, formula} checked by proof_steps_check. Nested proof terms: one answer with a nested term [rule, …] checked by proof_check. sections: How candidates are scored and which one wins.

Per case: score = max_score if the exact output equals expected and all checks passed, else 0. Per candidate: utility = score_weight x score sum - call_weight x charged calls - cost_weight x charged cost. The highest utility among eligible candidates wins; ties go to the smallest policy hash. Held-out improvement is established only when accounting is complete, the winner differs from the baseline and its utility gain is > 0 and >= min_heldout_gain x number of held-out cases.

Cost unit is provider_calls (every issued model call, including failures). A missing assignment is charged budget.max_calls; unknown cost makes a candidate ineligible when unknown_cost is reject (charged the budget when 'budget').

sections: A cheat sheet of the core statements: program, note, given, let, define, group, fact, rule, ask, ensure, assert, if/else, for, show, draw, forget, pin, delegate.

One statement per line with an optional final period; a statement continues while a bracket or string is open, after a trailing backslash, or onto lines that start with with/from/by/where/for each (SPEC §1). Names are bound once per scope. given = an input (required when it has no default); let = a kernel binding; define = a named type; group = named applicators with optional weights; fact = a ground Datalog fact; rule = a Horn rule whose Uppercase names are logic variables (stratified negation, range-restricted); ask = the model statement; ensure's default failure action is retry (parser symblic/kernel/language.py:1395), else fail/warn on request; assert/expect fail the run; names bound inside a for loop become lists after end; forget hides a value from later contexts but keeps it usable by name and by `from`; pin raises its context weight; delegate starts a host agent and needs side effects allowed.
Syntax only. The full grammar is available from a terminal: `bin/symblic grammar export --entry program --format ebnf`.

Typical Check errors: 'NAME is bound twice (Symblic names are immutable)'; 'sum is a builtin function name' (a let/given/ask result may not use a builtin's name, e.g. sum, count, cube); 'a fact must be ground: Who is a logic variable (write a rule for a general statement)'; 'expected the instruction in quotes' (put the quoted instruction on the ask line, not alone on the next line); "unexpected character '?'". The cheat sheet puts several statements on one line for compactness; type each on its own line.

program Hello.
given n: Int = 3.
let doubled = n * 2.
assert doubled = 6.
show doubled as "twice n".

sections: Syntax for functions, routines, imports, terms and tests (the abstraction layer).

function = one typed kernel expression (recursion up to 32 calls); in verified it may not reach a routine or adapter even indirectly. routine = a typed model function: every call runs its body in a fresh scope that cannot see the caller, its asks take the normal capsule/vote/ensure path, options after `with` are defaults only inside it, and within one run the same closure + arguments + defaults reuse the recorded value (a memo, not a new vote). A routine call must be its own statement (`let x = r(...)`). import loads a declarations-only module from symblic_lib/NAME.sym or a saved program; its source and SHA-256 go to the run's modules.json so resume/replay use the same text. term attaches its definition to every ask whose text uses the word. test blocks are skipped in runs and executed by Run tests (kernel only) or certify (with agents).

sections: The Symblic statement that READS the world through one declared capability (a the fleet layer read tool) and names the result.

`observe NAME [: TYPE] = family.name(arg=value, ...) [with OPTIONS].` In a the host runner run the kernel evaluates each argument, checks it against the capability's JSON Schema, writes and syncs an intent row in effects.jsonl, calls the fleet layer POST /api/fleet/tools/try (read + auto tools; a 403 there falls back to the proposal route), and binds the result {text, data}. A TYPE coerces it like a model answer (records keep only the named fields). It never changes anything. Outside a the host runner run it cannot execute (see automations.where_effects_run).

Identity = SHA-256 of [2, capability, canonical arguments, key]: the same read with the same arguments is performed once per ledger and a resume, retry or replay takes the recorded result. The value carries evidence {mechanism: observation, capability, effect_id, args_sha256, result_sha256, acquired_at, trusted_acquisition: true, independence: not_established} and determinism class "observed" (fixed inside a run). Untrusted capabilities (web pages, search results, mail, agents' answers) label the value untrusted; non-public ones label it personal (see lang.flow_labels). Every capability returns {text, data}: text is one human sentence, data is the tool's JSON. Compute from data with let; do not ask a model about text, which may not hold the answer (the first live the host runner run answered "offline: none" from the one-line text).

NAME required. TYPE optional, e.g. Record {data: Record {items: List of Record {id: Text, online: Bool}}}; a field that can be empty is typed Any (Text refuses an empty answer). Capability: lower-case dotted family.name with named arguments only. Options (with ...): key, scope (run | program), timeout (seconds), mode and sources (evidence labels), weight. allow_untrusted is act-only. Not allowed inside function, routine or test.
In /runner: a "reads" row in the program's effects list, a "read" row in "What it touched", a Steps row "observe <name>", and the value wherever you `show` it.

topics.title: Act
topics.where: symblic/kernel/effects.py:279-322 (parse), 372-407 (check), 1443-1654 (execute); host host_runner.py:193-302 (proposal, mission polling, approvals).
sections: The Symblic statement that CHANGES something through one declared capability (effect compute, write-local, write-external, device, destructive or money).

`act [NAME [: TYPE] =] family.name(arg=value, ...) [with key="...", scope=program, ...].` In a the host runner run with side effects allowed: arguments are evaluated and schema-checked, an intent row is synced, the host proposes the action to the fleet layer (POST /api/personal-agent/action/propose with request id "fx" + effect id[:36] + failure count, in one conversation per run, or per program for scope=program) and polls the fleet layer mission every 2 s. If the fleet layer parks an approval in its inbox, the host runner approves it itself (full mode, or guarded with "Approve guarded actions by itself") or the run shows "Waiting for you". The outcome row (done, failed or unknown) is written and a named result binds like an observation.

At most one automatic performance per identity. With a key the identity is the key alone (SHA-256 of [2, capability, null, key]), so `with key="digest-{today}"` happens once per key whatever its arguments say later; without a key it is capability + arguments. An interrupted action is continued under the same request id (same the fleet layer mission), never started twice; an unknown outcome of a non-idempotent action stops the run as "uncertain" until you say whether it happened. An act may not stand between an ask and the ensure that may re-ask it. Untrusted text may not be an argument (lang.flow_labels). An action whose the fleet layer mission is still running after its timeout (the statement's timeout option, else the tool's declared timeout, else 3600 s; time spent waiting for approval excluded) is recorded as unknown.

NAME and TYPE optional. Options: key (text, recommended whenever the same call could repeat), scope = run (default) or program (needs a key and a saved program's run), timeout (seconds), allow_untrusted=["arg"] (carry outside text in that argument; never for capabilities that instruct an agent or program), mode, sources, weight.

Program panel: a "changes" row (+ "asks you" in guarded mode when it will wait). Run screen: "Waiting for you" card while the fleet layer waits; afterwards a "changed" row in "What it touched" with the fleet layer's result text, or a phase tag "in progress", "failed", "unknown".

Pass it through a closed type (a choice, Bool, a small Int range)"; "scope=program needs a key: it names the action across runs"; warning "<cap> only reads: observe says so and needs no side effects"; run-time "act <cap>: the outcome is unknown (...). It may have happened; effect <12 hex> needs the owner's word before a rerun", "act <cap> failed: <the fleet layer error>". the fleet layer refusals before a mission exists (bad arguments, not allowed) are definite failures.

key: a text (evaluated at run time, so "digest-{today}" interpolates) naming the action. scope: run (one ledger per run) or program (every run of the same saved program shares host_runner/ledgers/<name>.<hash>.jsonl, so "once a day" holds across runs and clock fires). timeout: seconds for this call (else the tool's own). mode and sources: author labels recorded in the value's evidence (records, not weights). weight: the binding's weight for later context selection. allow_untrusted (act only): argument names allowed to carry outside text.

sections: The information-flow rules that keep outside text from writing an action and personal data from leaving the house.

Every value gets labels from the program text alone: untrusted (from untrusted capabilities: web.search, web.read, lit.search, mail.*, agents.result/report, runner.status, answers from the host's other agents ...), steered (untrusted passed through a closed type, or a condition/loop over it), personal (from non-public capabilities). Warning: an ask shown personal data. A steered weighty act (write-external, device, destructive, money, or one that instructs an agent or program) is marked needs_owner.

Static, per statement and conservative: labels follow let, facts, asks (by interpolation, from, wide context), function and routine bodies, branches and loops. A closed type (Bool, one of {...}, a small Int range) limits outside text to choosing among alternatives the program wrote. In guarded mode a needs_owner action always waits unless "Also when outside text chose the action" is on; full mode approves it. An argument outside text WROTE (allow_untrusted) is approved only in full mode.

sections: The append-only record of every read and action a run made, which lets a run resume without repeating actions.

Before each call an intent row is written and synced; after it an outcome row: done (with result and hashes), failed (nothing happened) or unknown (it may have happened). sections: A workflow step that runs one Symblic program inside an Automation Studio workflow.

When the workflow reaches the node, the Studio runner (a thread of the host process) builds an in-memory Symblic run of the Program text with the workflow's variables as inputs and the Default agent as the default applicator (parallel 3, at most 200 asks), executes it, and on success turns every top-level result into a variable symblic_<name> plus symblic_fingerprint; the node's output (last_output) is the text of its show/return lines joined by newlines, or "Symblic done (fingerprint <hex>)". Kernel lines run in the host process; ask lines go to models through the fleet layer (CLIs and Ollama on the worker nodes, browser chats on the host). It never performs observe, act or delegate, and keeps no run folder: nothing to resume or replay.

No capability host and no side effects are passed, so observe fails "no capability host is connected: observe <cap> cannot run here", act fails "act <cap> changes something: run the program with side effects allowed" and delegate fails "delegate starts an agent: run the program with side effects allowed" (probe-confirmed). A failure raises "Symblic <status>: line N: <message>"; the step is recorded as error with an empty output, and the workflow CONTINUES to the next node (the run still ends "completed"). sections: A saved workflow of exact native Symblic programs, durable owner state, bounded waits, delays and joins. the host runner runs the programs and the fleet layer keeps the clock. Reconnecting to the browser does not start another firing.

Load example, Save workflow, then Run once. Two independent exact calculations start; a join waits for their successful completion. The example checks owner state and increments a counter. Refresh shows saved state; Advance once reconciles known native runs.

A delay waits at least its declared seconds. A wait checks an owner-state or step-status condition until within_s expires. Schedule with the fleet layer creates recurring firings using five-field cron. The minute reconciliation pulse is durable; it is not a subsecond sleep and may be late under load. Native finite for loops remain available inside each step.

An unknown outcome, damaged native journal or expired native deadline cannot authorize compensation. Open the native record and reconcile only an exact matching handle. Pause stops future supervisor transitions but leaves already submitted native children alone. Disable the recurring schedule separately when you want no new firings.

Simulation uses supplied synthetic statuses and performs no native execution. Model answers and event payloads are never copied into trusted owner state. Native programs retain their own checks, flow labels and admitted effects. Saved source, inputs, runtime versions and permission ceilings are frozen; changing a program means saving a new workflow.
